evals.prompt: Using only the supplied Microsoft eShopOnContainers evidence fixture, apply build-signal-graph to create the complete authoritative TypeScript Signal model for checkout through final order outcome, then apply render-signal-graph to produce a self-contained architecture/index.html. Model HTTP 202 acceptance separately from asynchronous processing; include web/mobile ingress, success, stock-rejection, and payment-failure flows; and do not invent fraud, card-network, shipping, or email services. Preserve signal.ts, architecture.ts, architecture/index.html, and validation results for inspection.
evals.expected_output: An inspectable, strictly type-checked TypeScript architecture and deterministic offline HTML projection derived from the same live object-reference model.
expectations: The saved artifacts include signal.ts, architecture.ts, architecture/index.html, and validation results with a successful strict TypeScript check and render command.

Web and mobile callers, distinct BFF/API gateways, Basket, Ordering, Catalog, Payment, Ordering SignalR Hub, Redis, separate relational stores, and event-bus infrastructure are modeled without invented fraud, card-network, shipping, or email services.

Basket checkout reads Redis, publishes UserCheckoutAcceptedIntegrationEvent, and returns HTTP 202 before any asynchronous order creation; asynchronous flows explicitly continue from acceptance rather than implying that the caller waits.

The successful continuation preserves idempotent Ordering dispatch, Ordering SQL persistence, Basket cleanup, Catalog validation and SQL update, stock confirmation, Payment handling, paid-state persistence, and SignalR status propagation in evidenced order.
Stock rejection and payment failure are separate linked flows that persist and propagate terminal cancelled outcomes.

HTTP, schemas, messages, topics, subscriptions, consumers, stores, publication, delivery, consumption, reads, writes, responses, contract derivations, and continuation links use typed object references without any or unsafe casts.
Disputable declarations and flows carry fixture evidence, unsupported dependencies are absent, and uncertainty is not presented as observed fact.

The generated output is one deterministic, self-contained HTML file with no external assets; it includes counts, directional topology, inventories, search/filtering, ordered flows, continuation links, contracts, schemas, and evidence.
All model-controlled HTML text is escaped, a restrictive CSP is present, unresolved object references fail rendering, and rendering the same model twice is byte-identical.

The handoff treats architecture.ts as authority and architecture/index.html as a disposable projection, with enough preserved output for human review and future version-to-version regression comparison.
